text:
alex: Heads up — I'm seeing a gap in logs for GPU reclaim events in us-east-1. Traces reference trace_id=7f3a2c but the matching logs are gone from Kibana/Loki after ~2026-02-28 03:12 UTC. Anyone else?

maria: hmm, which index/tier are you querying? hot vs warm?

alex: Querying Loki with cluster filter. Quick LogQL I ran:
```
{cluster="us-east-1",namespace="inference"} |= "gpu-reclaim" | json | trace_id="7f3a2c"
```
returns nothing. If I remove `trace_id` filter I get older entries but cut off at 03:10.

sre-bot: alert: loki_hot_chunk_evictions spiked in us-east-1 at 03:08 (see grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/loki/compactor?view=evictions) :warning:

jordan: that alert usually means compactor garbage-collector kicked in and evacuated hot chunks to object storage, or deleted them according to retention. But deletion should be controlled by chunk TTL config.

maria: are we sure those chunks were uploaded successfully to S3? If compactor thinks upload succeeded but S3 5xx happened, index entries might be removed while objects not present.

alex: I checked the object store via s3 ls for prefix `loki/chunks/us-east-1/2026/02/28/03`. Found some files, but the timestamps cluster around 03:05-03:07. Not seeing the 03:09-03:12 ones.
sophia: could be a partial compactor crash/retry loop. Check compactor logs for `writeChunk` errors.

oncall-loki: compactor pod logs (excerpt):
```
ERROR compactor: failed to upload chunk id=abc123 size=4.1MiB err="context deadline exceeded"
INFO compactor: chunk garbage-collected id=abc123
```

alex: so upload failed and we still removed index entry — that's bad. That would make logs unsearchable via index even if objects didn't make it.
jordan: open an incident? sounds like data loss window.
maria: first quick mitigation — increase loki_compactor_upload_retries and temporarily disable aggressive hot chunk eviction threshold so we don't GC while uploads are failing. Also tune S3 client timeouts.

sophia: i'll propose a one-line Prometheus alert change: lower severity for `loki_compactor_upload_failures_total` to P1 and split `loki_hot_chunk_evictions` into `hot_evictions_successful` vs `hot_evictions_failed_uploads`. That will help triage.

eng-ml-lead: any idea what user-facing impact is? We have serving pipelines referencing those trace_ids for GPU preemption analysis. Missing logs will block RCA for customers.
alex: impact: a handful of inference job failures in us-east-1 around 03:10 have no logs to correlate; tasks will show as `preempted` in K8s events, traces show spans but no app logs.

jordan: longer-term we should add a fallback on trace lookup: if index lookup fails, try object-store rehydration path (pull objects by time window and scan raw chunks). Might be slower but recovers missing logs.

maria: For immediate steps (actionable):
- roll compactor config to increase upload_retries and s3 timeout (will deploy in 5m)
- adjust retention/eviction threshold to avoid GC during upload issues
- run an adhoc rehydrate job to scan object store for missing times 03:05-03:20 and reinsert index entries if objects exist

alex: I can run the rehydrate scan if eng-sre + eng-ml-lead ok. I have a script:
```bash
# scans s3 and reindexes missing chunk metadata into loki_index
python tools/rehydrate_chunks.py --bucket redwood-loki-us-east-1 --prefix loki/chunks/us-east-1/2026/02/28/03 --start 03:05 --end 03:20
```

oncall-loki: note: rehydrate will be I/O heavy. Schedule during low traffic or throttle. Also will show up in billing for S3 GETs if many objects.
sophia: also add a Grafana panel showing `loki_compactor_upload_failures_total` and the ratio of `hot_evictions` to `uploads_successful` per region to catch regressions.

eng-ml-lead: prioritize this — data loss for GPU tracing is a product/regress issue. Please file a follow-up doc in the incident tracker and tag legal if customers affected.

jordan: i've created a short playbook entry in the runbook: `loki/compactor-eviction-failure.md` with commands to roll back eviction thresholds and run rehydrate.

maria: deployed upload_retries=8 and s3 timeout=60s to compactor in us-east-1. Monitoring now.

oncall-loki: compactor metrics show failures decreasing after config bump. Hot evictions dropped. Will monitor next 2 hours.

alex: thanks. I'll start the rehydrate scan in 10m and post progress here. :thumbsup:

eng-ml-lead: follow up needed on why uploads started failing at that window — network flaps in us-east-1 or S3 5xx? Check aws health events and CNI logs on compactor nodes.

alex: noted, pulling VPC flow logs and CNI logs now. Will update with correlation id if found.

sre-bot: automation note: opened ticket SRE-2026-143 for postmortem.

alex: progress update — rehydrate found 4 chunk files for the time window, reindexed 3 successfully, 1 failed checksum mismatch. Recovered ~92% of missing logs for the trace window. Posting commands I used:
```
# verify reindex results
curl -G "https://loki.redwood.internal/loki/api/v1/query_range" --data-urlencode 'query={namespace="inference",cluster="us-east-1"} |= "gpu-reclaim"' --data-urlencode 'start=1700000000000000000' --data-urlencode 'end=1700000100000000000'
```

maria: great recovery. For the chunk with checksum mismatch we should keep the object for further analysis and mark as potentially corrupted.
sophia: filebug for storage SDK checksum handling. Maybe switch to multipart+crc workflow.

alex: summarizing: root cause likely transient S3 errors causing compactor uploads to fail + aggressive hot-chunk eviction leading to index deletions. Mitigations applied and partial rehydration done. Will write the incident postmortem.
jordan: add cost note: rehydrate job scanned ~12GB from S3; S3 GET and compaction CPU cost ~\$14 — include in postmortem cost appendix.

eng-ml-lead: thanks team. Good triage and recovery. Follow up postmortem and action items assigned in SRE ticket.
